skill.name: building-mcp-servers
skill.description: Guides development of MCP servers in Python or TypeScript, including tool design, transports, authentication, deployment, testing, and evaluation.
skill.summary: Build practical MCP servers and evaluate how reliably AI agents use their tools.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown, template strings, placeholders, or documented API examples. Two exposure patterns and three semantic design risks remain confirmed.

remediation.issue: Remote MCP examples lack client authentication and use broad network settings.
remediation.suggestion: Require OAuth or signed gateway identity, restrict origins and hosts, and bind only to an intended private interface.

remediation.issue: Access tokens and API keys appear in tool parameters and command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Keep credentials in server-side secret storage, inject them outside model-visible schemas, and redact logs and evaluation reports.

remediation.issue: Untrusted MCP tool descriptions and results enter the model loop without isolation.
remediation.suggestion: Evaluate only trusted servers in a sandbox, use limited credentials, restrict tool permissions, and require confirmation for consequential actions.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Remote MCP Endpoints
semantic_findings.description: Remote examples expose MCP handlers without client authentication. Permissive CORS and broad binding can make upstream capabilities reachable by unauthorized clients.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly omit MCP client authentication, allow every CORS origin, and bind the TaskFlow server to all interfaces.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials Exposed as Tool and CLI Inputs
semantic_findings.description: The guidance puts access tokens in model-visible tool parameters and accepts secrets through command arguments. Transcripts, logs, or process listings may expose them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented tool schema includes access_token, while evaluation examples place API keys and authorization headers directly on the command line.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted MCP Content Re-enters Agent Loop
semantic_findings.description: The evaluator sends server-defined tools and tool results directly to the model. A malicious server can inject instructions or influence later tool calls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Tool schemas and returned content cross directly into model requests without server trust checks, content isolation, or confirmation controls.

content.value_statement: MCP server projects often lack consistent tool design, transport choices, and evaluation methods. This skill provides practical Python and TypeScript patterns for implementation and testing.
actual_capabilities: Plans MCP tools around service APIs, workflows, naming, schemas, pagination, and response formats.
Provides Python FastMCP and TypeScript MCP SDK implementation patterns.
Explains stdio, Streamable HTTP, authentication, error handling, Docker deployment, and health checks.
Includes a Python harness for XML-based evaluations using Claude and connected MCP tools.
Provides a verification script that checks required reference files.
limitations: It does not deploy, host, or operate an MCP server automatically.
Example code requires adaptation for each service, permission model, and production environment.
The evaluation harness requires Anthropic and MCP Python dependencies plus a valid API key.
Some remote-server examples require stronger authentication, credential handling, and network restrictions before production use.

use_cases.title: Create a Service Integration
use_cases.description: Design and implement an MCP server that exposes a service API through clear, validated tools.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Production Deployment
use_cases.description: Choose transports, container settings, authentication boundaries, health checks, and operational safeguards for an MCP service.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agent Tool Use
use_cases.description: Create stable read-only tasks and measure whether an agent can use MCP tools to produce verified answers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic MCP Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python FastMCP server for [service]. List tools, input schemas, response formats, authentication needs, and a minimal test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a TypeScript Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript MCP server design for [API]. Include Zod schemas, pagination, structured responses, error handling, and stdio transport.

prompt_templates.title: Create Evaluation Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop ten independent read-only evaluation questions for this MCP server. Make each answer stable, verifiable, realistic, and difficult enough to require tools.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Remote Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Streamable HTTP MCP design for authentication, authorization, secret handling, prompt injection, origin validation, network exposure, rate limits, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a project management API.
output: A prioritized tool catalog for projects, tasks, users, and status updates.
Validated input and output requirements for every tool.
A transport, authentication, pagination, and error-handling plan.

output_examples.input: Review this remote MCP deployment before production.
output_examples.output: The review identifies authentication gaps, broad network exposure, secret-handling risks, missing rate limits, and focused remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation coverage for a repository MCP server.
output_examples.output: Ten read-only tasks cover search, comparison, aggregation, historical analysis, pagination, failure handling, and exact answer verification.

best_practices: Use narrowly scoped tools with validated schemas, precise descriptions, pagination, and structured outputs.
Keep credentials outside model-visible inputs and enforce authorization for every remote request.
Test valid, invalid, adversarial, and high-volume inputs with stable read-only evaluations.
anti_patterns: Do not expose remote MCP handlers without client authentication, origin controls, and restricted network binding.
Do not place access tokens, API keys, or sensitive user data in tool schemas or command arguments.
Do not trust tool annotations or server-returned content as security guarantees.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python with FastMCP and TypeScript with the official MCP SDK.

faq.question: Does it build a complete server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides design and implementation, while the developer adapts examples to the target service.

faq.question: Which transports are included?
faq.answer: It covers stdio for local integrations and Streamable HTTP for remote or multi-client deployments.

faq.question: Can it evaluate an MCP server?
faq.answer: Yes. The included Python harness runs XML-defined tasks through Claude and records accuracy, timing, tool usage, and feedback.

faq.question: Is the example remote configuration production-ready?
faq.answer: No. Add client authentication, strict authorization, origin validation, secret protection, rate limits, and restricted network binding.

faq.question: Does the evaluator support Codex or Claude Code models?
faq.answer: The marketplace guidance supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, but the bundled evaluation harness directly uses the Anthropic client.
